ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in parallelogram $ABCD$, point $M$ is the midpoint of $CD$, and $AM$ intersects $BD$ at point $N$. If it is known that the area of $\triangle DMN$ is 3, then what is the area of $\triangle ADN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since point $M$ is the midpoint of $CD$, \\
$\therefore$ DM=$\frac{1}{2}CD$, \\
In parallelogram $ABCD$ where AB$\parallel$CD, AB=CD, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ABN=$\angle$MDN, $\angle$BAN=$\angle$DMN, \\
$\therefore$ $\triangle ABN\sim \triangle MDN$, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AB}{MD}=\frac{AN}{MN}=\frac{CD}{DM}=2$, \\
$\therefore$ AN=2MN, \\
$\therefore$ $\frac{{S}_{\triangle ADN}}{{S}_{\triangle DMN}}=AN:MN=2:1$, \\
Since ${S}_{\triangle DMN}=3$, \\
$\therefore$ ${S}_{\triangle ADN}=2{S}_{\triangle DMN}=2\times 3=\boxed{6}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, quadrilateral ABCD can be seen drawn as a parallelogram, with A and B above, D and C below, and AB parallel to CD; point M is located on the bottom side CD; segment AM connects from A to M, and intersects the diagonal BD from D to B at point N. Then reason: It is known that M is the midpoint of CD, so DM = CD/2. Because ABCD is a parallelogram, AB ∥ CD and AB = CD; also, DM is on CD, therefore AB ∥ DM, and AB/DM = CD/(CD/2) = 2. Since A, N, M are collinear, B, N, D are collinear, and AB ∥ DM, it can be obtained that ∠ABN = ∠MDN, ∠BAN = ∠DMN, so △ABN ∼ △MDN. From the similarity ratio, AN/MN = AB/DM = 2, that is, AN = 2MN. The base sides AN and MN of triangle ADN and triangle DMN are both on the same straight line AM, and they have the same height from D to AM, therefore the area ratio S△ADN : S△DMN = AN : MN = 2 : 1. It is known that S△DMN = 3, so S△ADN = 2 × 3 = 6.
